A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CreditDecoding. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original eight-benchmark evaluations on two LLaDA models, hyperparameter and block-size ablations, decoding-trace analyses, and optimization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds model comparisons, decoding-strategy evaluations, ablations, confidence analyses, and benchmark-specific throughput measurements.

M1.justification: The default credit recurrence and logit fusion remain unchanged. Section 4.3 adds an optional adaptive schedule with alpha_t = beta_t = 1 - mask_ratio and gamma = 1; Appendix C.9 adds top-K credit-update variants. Algorithm 1 also specifies greedy commits instead of v1's categorical sampling. The full-distribution variant is retained in Appendix C.8.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, SQuAD2.0, DROP, KorBench, HumanEval, LiveCodeBench, GSM8K, and MATH, with the same five-dataset subset for supplementary experiments. Added model and decoding configurations do not introduce distinct datasets, tasks, or populations.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds auxiliary comparisons against fixed Top-K decoding, with K = 2, 4, and 8, and Top-K margin decoding, each evaluated with and without credit. v1 mentioned these options without reporting these comparisons. Fast-dLLM and the existing optimization comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 adds SDAR-8B, LLaDA2-Mini, and LLaDA2-Flash evaluations, extending model configurations to 100B parameters and reporting generation length 2048, block size 32, and dInfer inference. New experiments also vary gamma and decoding-selection rules. The original Table 1 length, step budget, block size, and Appendix B scoring and few-shot settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds gamma sensitivity testing (Figure 7), top-K credit reinforcement ablations (Table 8), temporal-consistency analysis grouped by denoising duration (Figure 4), a contextual cumulative-effect case study (Figure 12), and selection-rule robustness tests (Table 3). Existing ablations largely remain after relocation, although v1 Figure 1's HumanEval decoding-boundary panel is absent from v2 Figure 9.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that each setting has single-run results and adds an overall mean plus/minus one standard deviation display for confidence trajectories in Figure 4. These are reporting additions, not evidence of increased runs or confidence intervals for benchmark improvements.

E6.justification: The original Table 1 scores and TPF values are retained, including CreditDecoding averages of 53.98/5.48 on LLaDA-8B and 55.57/4.11 on LLaDA-MoE. The full-distribution results move to Tables 6–7. Substantial new results appear in Tables 2, 3, 8, and 9; for example, Table 9 reports average TPS of 32.72 versus Fast-dLLM's 27.50. These are additional evaluations, not improved versions of the retained scores.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C.1 add a derivation of the single-token logit gain required to cross a confidence threshold: X_min = tau(1-p)/((1-tau)p). v1 only explained the multiplicative effect of credit fusion. v2 also omits the explicit background training-loss equation while retaining the underlying transition and credit mathematics.

C1.justification: The central training-free acceleration claim and headline 5.48-fold speedup with +0.48 performance remain. v2 adds tuning-free usability as a contribution and explicit claims about generality across model paradigms and parameter scales. It removes the conclusion's claim of exploiting remasked-token predictions 'for the first time.'

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability boundaries: insufficient credit accumulation with short traces, task/model-dependent tuning, and reasoning or coding failures (Limitations and Appendix C.11). It also develops low-pass filtering, contextual feedback, and focused-versus-distributed credit explanations. v1 contained narrower discussions of confidence fluctuations and hyperparameter/block-size tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 discloses gamma = 0.2, tuning on LLaDA-8B, the numerical threshold in Table 3, dInfer for the added model study, and more explicit per-block tensor operations in Algorithm 1. Hardware, OpenCompass, and few-shot configurations were already documented. The gamma disclosure does not establish a change to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SDAR, LLaDA2.0, and dInfer. It also qualifies the characterization of prior score-based methods as history-agnostic and removes the first-use priority assertion. The broader related-work framework remains similar; bibliographic updates do not represent additional research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. The full-distribution variant and several trace analyses move into an expanded appendix, while the main text gains generalizability, versatility, and limitations sections. Terminology, author affiliations, and supporting statements also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and redraws the method schematic. It splits the orthogonality/scalability figure, combines the alpha/beta plots and orthogonality tables, restructures the main and full-distribution result tables, and relocates or enlarges trace figures. Several genuinely new figures and tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for portability and design choices that v1 evaluated mainly on two related LLaDA models. Cross-paradigm evaluations up to 100B parameters, selection-rule comparisons, and targeted credit ablations address important evidential gaps; disclosed hyperparameters and specific limitations improve reproducibility and interpretation. Some claims remain overstated: Table 2's adaptive LLaDA-8B score is 60.23 versus Fast-dLLM's 60.38, and single-run results leave small accuracy gains uncertain. These weaknesses temper, but do not outweigh, the stronger empirical and explanatory support.
